acceptedDecisions.title: Pane runtime state: how process, status, cwd and git are detected and published (locked 2026-06-18)
acceptedDecisions.decision:
Source: sections 0.1-0.8 of the old pane-runtime-state plan (a planning file, now a historical archive). Condensed, nothing dropped on purpose.

0.1 State and events. One source of truth: the backend/pane in heca-core owns the runtime truth (program, exit, cwd). The chrome store (heca/src/chrome/state.rs) holds a reactive mirror that widgets subscribe to. Session stays canonical. Every change goes through ONE mutation point that notifies two channels: (1) internal floem_reactive signals so heca's own widgets repaint, and (2) a typed event bus so plugins and providers react with app.on(name, handler). Plugins cannot subscribe to internal signals (especially future WASM), so the bus is mandatory. The bus is built now. Events are typed per slice (pane.process.changed, pane.status.changed, pane.exited, chrome.region.changed, selection.changed) and reach plugins as string names plus a catch-all (app.on('*' | 'updated', ...)).

0.2 Detection is event-first, no polling timer. Exit: PTY child-wait / reader EOF is the event (child.try_wait()); no poll. Command success/error and cwd arrive as escape sequences in the output: OSC 133 (semantic prompts) and OSC 7 (cwd). For a directly spawned single command the exit code comes straight from the child; OSC 133 is only for commands run inside an interactive shell pane. Foreground program and running/idle has no clean OS event, so it is re-sampled on every terminal-output wake and on OSC 133 command start/end markers, rate-limited by a 250 ms debounce so output bursts do not hammer tcgetpgrp/libproc. No periodic timer: the 250-500 ms poll fallback is deferred and added only if testing shows silent foreground changes (programs that start/exit with no output) are missed. Exit is the reader's EOF wake then try_wait. Git is re-checked on a cwd change (OSC 7) plus an optional .git filesystem watch, slow-debounced; never per tick.

0.3 Display. Fixed default pane-info display built as real heca-grid-ui widgets, theme driven. Row 1 is the program: icon, name, optional exceptional-state indicator (idle shell shows the terminal icon plus the shell name; a running program shows its catalog icon plus display name). Row 2 is git, only inside a git repo: branch label plus optional +N / ~N / -N counters. Status set is Running, Idle, Success, Error. There is NO Exit status (see 0.6). Success and Error come from OSC 133. Idle and Running do not render a token in the compact row; only exceptional states surface. The process catalog is a user-extensible [program.<id>] map giving name, icon, description, color (see 0.7). Deferred: tmux-style ${token} templates; agreed shape when built is the hybrid model (a list of widget-typed segments, each a ${token} template). Update 2026-06-20 (Phase 7): the design landed as an in-pane segmented info bar (a Tag in the pane top), not a sidebar-corner badge. Segment-list selection was pulled forward as plain config ([appearance] pane_title_segments / pane_title_actions); only ${token} templating remains deferred. Bottom placement is a future flag.

0.4 Command spawn. WmAction::SpawnCommand (then a stub that only titled the pane) becomes a real launch via CommandBuilder, placed tiled or floating, remembering its close policy. [[keys.command]] grows the keys: key, command, kind ("terminal" now, "app"/"plugin" later), float, close_pane, keep_on_error, keep_on_success. close_pane is the master switch; keep_on_error / keep_on_success are per-outcome overrides applied when pane.exited fires (exit code from the child).

0.5 Git library. git2 (libgit2) behind a small GitProvider trait so swapping to gix later is one file. Reason: mature, complete statuses() plus branch/ahead-behind.

0.6 Pane lifetime and close. A pane lives as long as its terminal: the shell (the PTY child portable_pty spawned). try_wait waits on that shell, not on programs inside it. Auto-close fires only when the shell dies. A foreground program (nvim, lazygit, yazi) exiting does NOT close the pane; status becomes Idle. There is no Exit status variant: a dead pane closes, so it has nothing to display. The exit code travels on the pane.exited{code} event. Close policy (keep_on_error / keep_on_success) applies only to direct-spawn panes ([[keys.command]] run as the PTY child, no shell). In Phase 2 every pane is a shell pane.

0.7 Process catalog [program.<id>]. Keyed by a canonical app id; fields name, processes (raw process aliases), icon (semantic Phosphor name, snake_case/kebab-case accepted), description (not rendered yet), color (optional tint); all optional. name falls back to the raw process name; icon falls back to the default terminal icon. [programs.<id>] stays as a compatibility alias. Shells (zsh/bash/fish/sh) are seeded with the terminal icon; user entries override same-key defaults. Resolver: ProgramsConfig::resolve(raw) -> ProgramView { raw, name, icon, color }.

0.8 Phase 3 shape (settled 2026-06-18). Shell hook is shell-specific wrapping, not a pure env var: bash uses --init-file with a heca snippet that sources ~/.bashrc then installs PROMPT_COMMAND + DEBUG/trap hooks emitting OSC 133 A/B/C/D and OSC 7; zsh sets ZDOTDIR to a heca dir whose .zshrc sources ${OLD_ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zshrc then installs precmd/preexec; fish uses fish -C "source <snippet>". Snippets live under assets/shell-integration/; pty.rs picks the flag/env per detected shell; document a manual install path. Config switch is one flat bool [settings] shell_integration = true (false = bare shell); grow to a [shell_integration] table only if needed later. OSC parsing is a passive pre-parse snooper in heca-core before engine.advance_bytes(): wezterm-term at pinned rev 891bed31 has no general OSC-dispatch callback. It scans bytes, extracts OSC 133/7, forwards ALL bytes unchanged. Minimal VT state machine: ESC ] collects until BEL (0x07) or ST (ESC \ or C1 0x9C); keeps a residual buffer across advance_bytes calls for fragmented OSC. Routing: OSC 133 D;0 = Success, D;!=0 = Error plus code; OSC 7 file://host/path = cwd; OSC 133 A/B/C trigger the foreground re-sample; all emitted through the single mutation point as pane.status.changed / pane.cwd.changed. Reason: no fork of wezterm's parser, one small unit-testable module, same approach other embedders use.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The plan file is now a historical archive, not maintained (T561), but code still depends on these rules: process detection must stay event-first, and a program exiting must not close the pane. Plugins need the event bus because they cannot see internal signals. The original file said "do not re-litigate".
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Two code comments cite the old file and must be re-pointed to this decision, because the old file is now a historical archive and not maintained: heca/src/app/process_monitor.rs:6 and heca-core/src/backend/terminal/process.rs:3 (both say "pane-runtime-state-plan.md section 0.2"). Related shipped work: P054(F006)/T176. Owner chosen: P054(F006) (plugin-observable pane state); no other phase owns process monitoring.
